candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes the classic KTS triad (capillary malformation, venous varicosities, and limb overgrowth/hypertrophy) plus syndactyly and lymphatic malformations. Diffuse lymphangiomatosis addresses only the lymphatic component identified on MRI and does not encompass the vascular and skeletal anomalies that define KTS as the unifying diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Lymphangiomatosis captures the extensive cystic lymphatic malformations seen on MRI but omits the defining composite features of Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome: port-wine capillary malformation, varicose/dilated veins, and limb hypertrophy/overgrowth with syndactyly

case_quality_flags: Extensive lymphatic malformations and pancreatic/splenic hemangiomas raise consideration of CLOVES or Proteus syndrome overlap; however, the classic KTS triad is well-represented and supports the reference diagnosis.
